Project objective

Transforming the fermentation outlet mixture into an industrial product.

The mixture produced through fermentation of corn starch does not directly contain high-purity ethanol. This design processes a feed stream containing approximately 10% ethanol through continuous distillation, increasing product purity up to the azeotropic limit.

Because ethanol is more volatile than water, the vapor rising through the column becomes richer in ethanol. The design jointly evaluates mass balances, the McCabe–Thiele method, tray efficiency and hydrodynamic limits.

Why 95.6%? Azeotropic limit

The ethanol-water system exhibits azeotropic behavior at approximately 95.6% ethanol composition under atmospheric pressure. Therefore, achieving higher purity through conventional distillation becomes difficult.

Main equipment

The four main components of the process.

The column body and auxiliary equipment work together to support continuous production.

01 · Separation

Distillation column

The main separation equipment, with a diameter of 1.264 m, a height of 9 m and 10 sieve trays.

  • AISI 304/316 stainless steel
  • Operation at atmospheric pressure
  • 70% tray efficiency
02 · Cooling

Shell-and-tube condenser

Converts the ethanol-rich vapor leaving the top of the column into a liquid phase and provides the reflux stream.

  • 15–20 m² heat transfer area
  • Condensation of ethanol-rich vapor
  • Reflux return line
03 · Heating

Kettle reboiler

Generates the vapor stream rising through the stages by heating the liquid at the bottom of the column.

  • Continuous vapor generation
  • High vapor capacity
  • Cleanable body structure
04 · Automation

PLC automation

Supports safe operation by monitoring flow rate, temperature and pressure variables in real time.

  • HMI touchscreen
  • Real-time data logging
  • Safety interlock system

Sustainability

Alternative fuel production from renewable resources.

Bioethanol is a renewable fuel that can serve as an alternative to fossil fuels. The continuously operating process approach provides advantages in terms of stable operating conditions and optimized energy use.
